sasha: Heads-up — after last night's deploy we see a big jump in cache misses on chat routes (high QPS). Hit rate on /generate dropped from ~88% -> ~65% for top-10 routes. Suspect combined tokenizer bump + small system prompt change.
jonathan: Oof. Do you have a sample pair (before vs after) that reproduces the miss? Could be whitespace or ordering in tool metadata.
sasha: Pasting sanitized examples (original = warmup population, new = live input after deploy):

```
# original (was in warmup)
{"user": "summarize this article", "system": "You are concise.", "tools": {"translate": true, "lookup": false}}

# live (post-deploy)
{"system": "You are concise.", "user": "summarize this article", "tools": {"lookup": false, "translate": true}}
```

Notice ordering changed for tools map and tokenizer v2.1 emits different whitespace+unicode normalizations.
kevin: That explains it. Our cache key pipeline currently serializes the raw request JSON (stable stringify? we thought) + model name. But we don't canonicalize dictionary ordering for tool fields; also tokenizer version is not part of key. So a reorder + tokenizer normalization can flip the key.
anya: We saw something similar in a customer case — tokenizer bumps changed punctuation splitting which altered the prefix tokenization and invalidated warmup. Two quick options: include (model, tokenizer_version, normalized_token_ids) in the key OR canonicalize the request structure and canonicalize text whitespace before hashing. Both have tradeoffs.
jonathan: Including token ids in the key makes keys model/tokenizer-specific (good), but increases key size and might make redis footprint bigger. Canonicalizing JSON + stable sort of tool keys is cheaper and preserves current cache entries for logically identical requests.
kevin: Proposal: two-pronged short-term / long-term plan: 
- Short-term hotfix: roll back the non-essential system prompt wording change for the 3 top routes, rewarm cache from last good snapshot, and deploy a deterministic canonicalizer for tool fields (stable sort keys + trim whitespace) — non-breaking and fast.
- Mid-term: change key schema to include model+tokenizer checksum and add a small token-prefix digest (e.g., first 40B of token-hash) to avoid collisions; keep backward compatibility by namespacing keys (v1/v2).

perf-bot: Regression alert: cache_miss_rate for /generate-chat-high dropped to 35% hit (prev 88%) at 2026-02-28T03:12:45Z — p50 latency +18% during the window.
sasha: I like the short-term approach. Who can run the warmup snapshot job? We have warmup artifacts from 2026-02-27 labelled warmup-snapshot-20260227 in s3.
anya: I can run warmup job and validate hit rates. Plan:
- Run canonicalizer patch behind feature flag (no key schema change) — 1 hour testing on canary (region us-west-2).
- If stable, rewarm using warmup-snapshot-20260227 and monitor hit rate delta.
- If hit rate recovers >80% for top routes, keep flag and schedule v2 key migration next week.
jonathan: For the canonicalizer, please ensure we: 
1) stable-sort JSON object keys (tools, metadata)
2) collapse repeated whitespace in system/user fields -> single space
3) normalize NFKC unicode for text fields
4) strip ephemeral tool debug fields (e.g., _trace_id) from keying
kevin: I'll prepare a minimal patch and unit tests for canonicalizer + a small benchmark script to prove we don't regress keying throughput. Canary target: 1% of traffic by EOD.
sasha: +1. Also add an instrumentation tag to cache entries from warmup so we can query "warmup=true" hit rate separately.
perf-bot: Canary run started: 1% traffic routed to canary-cluster-7 at 2026-02-28T04:05:10Z. Initial hit rate on canary: 79% (warmup in progress).
anya: I'll follow up with a short postmortem once we confirm root cause and finish warmup. Thanks all — assigning tasks:
- kevin: canonicalizer patch + bench (PR today)
- anya: run warmup-snapshot and monitor
- jonathan: add tokenization/version instrumentation to logs (non-blocking)
- sasha: coordinate rollback if warmup fails
jonathan: One more note — let's capture a small canonical test-set of 10k requests used for warmup and preserve it versioned (md5 + human-readable name) so future tokenizer bumps have a deterministic rewarm baseline.
sasha: Agreed. Creating ticket INF-512 for follow-up items. I'll post results here when warmup finishes. :thumbsup:
